newsitem.title: GUYANA: CRICKET-TENDULKAR, DRAVID MISS OUT ON CENTURIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TENDULKAR, DRAVID MISS OUT ON CENTURIES.

text.p: India's Sachin Tendulkar and Rahul Dravid both missed out on centuries against the West Indies Sunday as play in the fifth and final test finally resumed after more than two days lost to rain.
Captain Tendulkar was out for 83 and Dravid for 92 on the fourth day as India progressed to 241 for four in their first innings of a match in which a draw is the only realistic outcome.
India, trailing 1-0 in the series, had plodded to 194 for two on Thursday and then saw any chance of levelling the series disappear when rain washed out play on Friday and Saturday.
A brief but torrential tropical shower early Sunday morning drenched the field again and play only began in mid-afternoon after four pitch inspections.
A Guyana Defence Force helicopter hovered over the field for more than an hour to help dry the outfield, although the pitch had not suffered any damage.
Umpires decided that 31 overs would be played after the re- start but play was eventually interrupted again, this time by bad light, after 24 overs.
Tendulkar, who resumed on 62, began by hitting a well-timed straight drive for four.
However, he was out 17 runs later when he mistimed another drive at his 231st ball and gave paceman Ian Bishop a return catch that ended his third wicket stand with Dravid at 163.
Dravid, resolute as ever and showing impeccable technique, had an escape on 83 when wicket-keeper Courtney Browne dropped a sharp chance when he deflected a ball down the leg side.
But in the last but one over of the day, Dravid chased a wide ball and sliced a catch to point fielder Carl Hooper off paceman Franklyn Rose.
At the close, Mohammad Azharuddin was not out on four and Nayan Mongia was still to get off the mark.
